Header: Cocoa swollen shoot virus (CSSV) Kokoo sasabro

Prevention: Remove alternative hosts ( Cola chlamydantha (Kra-bise), Ceiba pentandra (Onyina), Adansonia digitata (Odadee), Cola gigantea (Watapuo) from cocoa farms
Divisions - as these offer some tolerance
Restrict movement of infected materials to disease-free areas
Use oil palm and citrus as barrier crops to restrict movement of the vector and reduce infection of new plantings adjacent to infected farms
Monitoring: CSSVD is vectored by mealybugs so monitor the field regularly for cocoa mealybugs ( Planococcoides njalensis and
It is usually the adult female which can be seen on pods and shoots.
These soft bodied and wingless insects produce a white waxy fluffy covering.
They are also associated with the production of honey dew and the growth of powdery black sooty mold
Monitor the cocoa trees regularly for symptoms of
CSSVD which are swollen chupons and fan branches, fern patterns, green banding and vein clearing on the leaves and the presence of round pods
If symptoms are observed on a single cocoa tree take immediate action
Direct Control: Eradicate all infected trees and contacted trees from plantations as soon as the symptoms are seen
Once removed, the infected plant should be burned.
The tree can be cut into pieces and used as fuel/fire wood
Remove the whole plant but do not cut it out, as this may result in rejuvenation of the old plant which may still carry the virus

Restrictions: There are no chemical pesticides to control this disease and
COCOBOD do not advise using pesticides to control mealybugs in cocoa
